description: Drum trigger sequencer: up to 25 named phrases of drum notes across ten voices, with per-note velocity, accents, ratchets, flams and probability, edited in a popup piano roll

params.text: Returns the playhead to the beginning, or to the start repeat marker with that option set on the menu
Starts and stops recording of the notes arriving at the record inputs into the current phrase
Clears every note out of the current phrase

inputs.text: The clock that drives playback, at four ticks per beat, which a clock module calls x4 or 1/16th
Chooses which of the 25 phrases plays, C3 selecting the first and the 25 semitones up to C5 the last; set to trigger on the menu it steps to the next non-empty phrase or picks one at random
A trigger returning the playhead to the beginning, or to the start repeat marker with that option set on the menu; playback carries on immediately if the sequencer is running
A trigger toggling between running and stopped; while stopped the gates are closed and clock ticks are ignored
Records drum notes from a keyboard, the ten white keys from C4 to E5 playing the ten voices
Records drum notes from a General MIDI drum kit, whose standard kit notes are mapped onto the ten voices
The note-on trigger for recording, taken from the gate output of a MIDI-CV module
Sets the velocity of each recorded note

outputs.text: A trigger on each note played by that voice
A trigger on each note of that voice that is marked as an accent in the editor
The velocity of the note being played by that voice
A trigger each time the playhead reaches the end of the phrase

notes: the large display draws the phrase with the playhead as a vertical line, and clicking it opens an editor for adding, moving and deleting notes and setting velocity, accent and probability
the small display names the phrase now playing, and clicking it lists the 25 phrases to choose from
a MIDI file can be imported from the editor or dragged onto it from disk, and the sequence exported to a MIDI file from there
a swing pattern set in the editor offsets quarter, eighth or sixteenth notes forwards or backwards by a chosen fraction, and a pattern set on a narrower part overrides a broader one
with Record enabled and Run switched off, each note played at the record inputs is written at the playhead, which then steps on by the quantisation amount
a new module holds no notes at all and plays nothing; click the large display to open the editor and add notes there, or record them from the record inputs
playback needs a clock patched to the clock input, at four ticks per beat, and the sequencer running; with no clock the playhead does not move and no gate opens
menu: Phrase selection input — chooses Pitch, C3-C5, Trigger next non-empty phrase, Trigger random phrase (random but fair), or Trigger random phrase (truly random)
Shared playhead — chooses Don't share the playhead, Shared playhead leader or Shared playhead follower, so several Entrian sequencers move their playheads together
Delay Clock/Reset/Run inputs — delays those three inputs by Auto, by None, or by a whole number of samples, to make up for the one-sample delay every cable adds
Set playhead to start marker on reset — sends a reset to the start repeat marker instead of to the beginning
Stop recording at end of song — ends recording when the playhead reaches the end, without a second press of Record
Automatically add repeat markers when recording — drops a start marker where recording began and an end marker where it stopped, and the playhead then loops that section
Save patch to use the free Entrian Player — writes a copy of the patch with every Entrian sequencer replaced by its play-only counterpart from the Entrian Free plugin
